name: Gitega

seo.title: Gitega travel guide - sights, stays & events
seo.description: Gitega, formerly Kitega, is the political capital of Burundi.
seo.twitterDescription: Gitega, formerly Kitega, is the political capital of Burundi.
seo.webpageDescription: Gitega, formerly Kitega, is the political capital of Burundi.

heroText: Gitega is Burundi's political capital and former royal seat, a highland city on the central plateau east of Bujumbura. First-time visitors should explore the National Museum of Gitega for royal regalia and drum culture, hear the sacred drums at the Gishora Royal Drum Sanctuary, and stroll the city's old cathedral quarter. Bujumbura International Airport, about 62 kilometres away, is the main gateway, since Gitega's own airfield has no scheduled passenger service.

areas.name: Centre Ville
areas.text: Centre Ville is Gitega's compact commercial core, with markets, shops and eateries within walking distance of the main government buildings.

areas.name: Near Gishora
areas.text: The area near Gishora, just outside the centre, is close to the Royal Drum Sanctuary and suits visitors focused on cultural and heritage sites.

airports.name: Bujumbura International Airport (BJM)
airports.text: Bujumbura International Airport, around 62 kilometres from Gitega, handles Burundi's international flights; plan for a road transfer of roughly ninety minutes to reach the capital.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Bujumbura International Airport (BJM) and central Gitega before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Stay in Centre Ville for walking access to markets, government offices and the National Museum, or base near Gishora for easier trips to the Royal Drum Sanctuary. Most visitors fly into Bujumbura and travel overland to Gitega.
hotelIntro: Gitega's hotel options are modest and concentrated in Centre Ville, the practical choice for most stays, while a base near Gishora suits travellers focused on the Royal Drum Sanctuary and surrounding heritage sites.
rentalCars: A hired car or driver is useful for the road transfer from Bujumbura and for reaching sites like Gishora outside the centre.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Centre Ville for easy walks to markets, government offices and the National Museum of Gitega.

travelTips.title: Getting there
travelTips.text: Fly into Bujumbura International Airport and budget around ninety minutes for the overland transfer to Gitega on the central plateau road.

travelTips.title: Museum hours
travelTips.text: Check opening hours for the National Museum and the Gishora Royal Drum Sanctuary in advance, since both can close for local events.

travelTips.title: Cash and language
travelTips.text: Carry Burundian francs for markets and small vendors, and expect French and Kirundi to be more widely used than English.

highlights.title: Gitega National Museum
highlights.text: Gitega National Museum is a key Gitega culture stop, useful for understanding local history, collections and rainy-day planning near the main sightseeing route.

highlights.title: Gitega Royal Palace
highlights.text: Gitega Royal Palace anchors the historic and ceremonial side of Gitega, making it a practical stop for architecture, local memory and orientation.

highlights.title: Gitega Cathedral

highlights.title: Gitega Market
highlights.text: Gitega Market gives Gitega a concrete street-life stop, with food, everyday shopping and local movement that helps visitors read the city.

highlights.title: Ruvubu National Park
highlights.text: Ruvubu National Park adds outdoor time to a Gitega stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

nearbyIdeas.text: Bujumbura is a nearby side trip from Gitega; keep it for a day when travel time, weather and opening hours fit the route.

nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: The Karera Falls are a scenic series of waterfalls in southern Burundi, a longer but rewarding day trip from Gitega for nature lovers.

history.text: The Germans laid out the plan for the modern town of Gitega in 1912 when Burundi was part of German East Africa.
Gitega was at one time the seat of the Kingdom of Burundi and remained as capital of the kings of Burundi (mwami) until 1966.

In March 2007, President of Burundi Pierre Nkurunziza announced that Burundi was planning to bring back its capital city to Gitega, saying that it is in a better location for a capital than Bujumbura.
On 24 December 2018, it was announced by Nkurunziza that Gitega was to become the capital city of Burundi, pending only Parliament approval.

The expected parliamentary assent (given the President's CNDD-FFD party comfortable majority in both chambers) arrived through a vote on 16 January 2019, with some ministries already starting the move two days later.
On 7 December 2021, a fire broke out in an overcrowded prison in Gitega, killing at least 38 and injuring more than 69.
